items.statement: Glove system materials for isolators and RABS are shown to have suitable mechanical and chemical resistance.
items.quote: The materials used for glove systems (for both isolators and RABS) should be demonstrated to have appropriate mechanical and chemical resistance.

items.statement: The glove replacement frequency is defined in the contamination control strategy (CCS).
items.quote: The frequency of glove replacement should be defined within the CCS.

items.statement: Isolator glove systems are leak tested with a method shown to suit the task and its criticality.
items.quote: For isolators, leak testing of the glove system should be performed using a methodology demonstrated to be suitable for the task and criticality.

items.statement: Isolator glove leak testing is carried out at defined intervals.
items.quote: The testing should be performed at defined intervals.

items.statement: Isolator glove integrity is tested at least at the start and end of each batch or campaign.
items.quote: Generally glove integrity testing should be performed at a minimum frequency of the beginning and end of each batch or campaign.

items.statement: Extra isolator glove integrity tests may be needed depending on the validated campaign length.
items.quote: Additional glove integrity testing may be necessary depending on the validated campaign length.

items.statement: Isolator glove integrity monitoring includes a visual check at each use and after any manipulation that could affect system integrity.
items.quote: Glove integrity monitoring should include a visual inspection associated with each use and following any manipulation that may affect the integrity of the system.

items.statement: For manual aseptic processing of single units or small batches, glove integrity verification frequency may be based on other criteria, e.g. start and end of each manufacturing session.
items.quote: For manual aseptic processing activities where single unit or small batch sizes are produced, the frequency of integrity verification may be based on other criteria, such as the beginning and end of each manufacturing session.
items.condition: manual aseptic processing of single unit or small batches

items.statement: Integrity/leak tests of isolator systems are performed at defined intervals.
items.quote: Integrity / leak testing of isolator systems should be performed at defined intervals.

items.statement: RABS gloves used in grade A are sterilised before installation and are sterilised or effectively bio-decontaminated by a validated method before each manufacturing campaign.
items.quote: For RABS, gloves used in the grade A area should be sterilised before installation and sterilised or effectively bio-decontaminated by a validated method prior to each manufacturing campaign.

items.statement: RABS gloves exposed to the background environment during operation are disinfected with an approved method after every exposure.
items.quote: If exposed to the background environment during operation, disinfection using an approved methodology following each exposure should be completed.
items.condition: if exposed to the background environment during operation

items.statement: RABS gloves are visually examined at each use.
items.quote: Gloves should be visually examined with each use

items.statement: RABS glove integrity testing is performed at periodic intervals.
items.quote: integrity testing should be performed at periodic intervals.

items.statement: Decontamination methods for RABS and isolators (cleaning, bio-decontamination and, where applicable, inactivation of biological materials) are appropriately defined and controlled.
items.quote: Decontamination methods (cleaning and bio-decontamination, and where applicable inactivation for biological materials) should be appropriately defined and controlled.

items.statement: Evidence exists that cleaning and bio-decontamination agents have no adverse impact on product made in the RABS or isolator.
items.quote: Evidence should also be available to demonstrate that the cleaning and bio-decontamination agents used do not have adverse impact on the product produced within the RABS or isolator.

items.statement: Isolator interior bio-decontamination is automated, validated, controlled within defined cycle parameters and uses a sporicidal agent in a suitable form (e.g. gas or vapour).
items.quote: The bio-decontamination process of the interior should be automated, validated and controlled within defined cycle parameters and should include a sporicidal agent in a suitable form (e.g. gaseous or vaporized form).

items.statement: During isolator bio-decontamination, gloves are extended with fingers separated so the agent contacts them.
items.quote: Gloves should be appropriately extended with fingers separated to ensure contact with the agent.

items.statement: Isolator cleaning and sporicidal bio-decontamination methods leave interior surfaces and the critical zone free of viable microorganisms.
items.quote: Methods used (cleaning and sporicidal bio-decontamination) should render the interior surfaces and critical zone of the isolator free from viable microorganisms.

i. For isolators

items.statement: RABS sporicidal disinfection includes routine application of a sporicidal agent by a validated method shown to cover all interior surfaces robustly and give a suitable environment for aseptic processing.
items.quote: The sporicidal disinfection should include the routine application of a sporicidal agent using a method that has been validated and demonstrated to robustly include all areas of the interior surfaces and ensure a suitable environment for aseptic processing.

items.statement: Cleanrooms and clean air equipment (UDAFs, RABS, isolators) used for sterile manufacture are qualified against the required environmental characteristics.
items.quote: Cleanrooms and clean air equipment such as unidirectional airflow units (UDAFs), RABS and isolators, used for the manufacture of sterile products, should be qualified according to the required characteristics of the environment.

items.statement: Each manufacturing operation has an appropriate environmental cleanliness level in the operational state to minimise contamination risk to product or materials handled.
items.quote: Each manufacturing operation requires an appropriate environmental cleanliness level in the operational state in order to minimize the risk of contamination of the product or materials being handled.

items.statement: Appropriate cleanliness levels are maintained in both the at rest and operational states.
items.quote: Appropriate cleanliness levels in the “at rest” and “operational” states should be maintained.

items.statement: Cleanrooms and clean air equipment are qualified using a methodology meeting Annex 15 requirements.
items.quote: Cleanrooms and clean air equipment should be qualified using methodology in accordance with the requirements of Annex 15.

items.statement: Cleanroom qualification, including classification, is clearly kept distinct from operational environmental monitoring.
items.quote: Cleanroom qualification (including classification) should be clearly differentiated from operational environmental monitoring.

items.statement: Where relevant to the installation's design or operation, cleanroom and clean air equipment qualification includes: installed filter leakage and integrity testing; airflow volume and velocity tests; air pressure difference test; airflow direction test and visualisation; microbial airborne and surface contamination; temperature test; relative humidity test; recovery test; containment leak test.
items.quote: As part of the qualification requirements of Annex 15, the qualification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment should include (where relevant to the design/operation of the installation): i. installed filter system leakage and integrity testing, ii. airflow tests - volume and velocity, iii. air pressure difference test, iv. airflow direction test and visualisation, v. microbial airborne and surface contamination, vi. temperature measurement test, vii. relative humidity test, viii. recovery test, ix. containment leak test.
items.condition: where relevant to the design/operation of the installation

items.statement: Cleanroom classification activities are scheduled and carried out so they do not affect process or product quality.
items.quote: Classification activities should be scheduled and performed in order to avoid any impact on process or product quality.

items.quote: For cleanroom classification, the total of particles equal to or greater than 0.5 and 5 µm should be measured.

items.statement: Classification particle measurements are made both at rest and in simulated operations against the Table 1 limits.
items.quote: This measurement should be performed both at rest and in simulated operations in accordance with the limits specified in Table 1.

items.statement: Classification may include 5 µm particles where the CCS or historical trends indicate it.
items.quote: Classification including 5µm particles may be considered where indicated by the CCS or historical trends.
items.condition: where indicated by the CCS or historical trends

items.statement: For grade D, the manufacturer sets in-operation particle limits from a risk assessment and, where applicable, routine data.
items.quote: The manufacturer should establish in operation limits based on a risk assessment and routine data where applicable.

items.statement: For classification of grade A and grade B areas, additional sampling locations beyond the ISO 14644-1 minimum are considered.
items.quote: For the aseptic processing area and the background environment (the grade A and grade B areas, respectively), additional sample locations should be considered
items.condition: grade A and grade B areas

items.statement: For classification of grade A and B areas, all critical processing areas such as the point of fill and container closure feeder bowls are evaluated.
items.quote: all critical processing areas such as the point of fill and container closure feeder bowls should be evaluated.
items.condition: grade A and grade B areas

items.statement: Critical processing locations are identified by documented risk assessment and knowledge of the process and operations in the area.
items.quote: Critical processing locations should be determined by documented risk assessment and knowledge of the process and operations to be performed in the area.

items.statement: Cleanroom classification is carried out in both the at rest and in operation states.
items.quote: Cleanroom classification should be carried out in the “at rest” and “in operation” states.

items.statement: The Table 1 at-rest total particle limits are met after a clean-up period following completion of operations and line clearance/cleaning.
items.quote: The total particle limits given in Table 1 above for the “at rest” state should be achieved after a “clean up” period on completion of operations and line clearance/cleaning activities.

items.statement: The clean-up period (guidance under 20 minutes) is determined during room qualification, documented, and followed in procedures to restore a qualified cleanliness state if disrupted during operation.
items.quote: The "clean up" period (guidance value of less than 20 minutes) should be determined during the qualification of the rooms, documented and adhered to in procedures to reinstate a qualified state of cleanliness if disrupted during operation.

items.statement: The air speed of unidirectional airflow systems, including where it is measured, is clearly justified in the qualification protocol.
items.quote: The speed of air supplied by unidirectional airflow systems should be clearly justified in the qualification protocol including the location for air speed measurement.

items.statement: Air speed is designed, measured and maintained so unidirectional air movement protects product and open components at the working position (e.g. where high-risk operations occur and product/components are exposed).
items.quote: Air speed should be designed, measured and maintained to ensure that appropriate unidirectional air movement provides protection of the product and open components at the working position (e.g. where high-risk operations occur and where product and/or components are exposed).

items.statement: Unidirectional airflow systems give a homogeneous air speed of 0.36 – 0.54 m/s (guidance value) at the working position unless otherwise scientifically justified in the CCS.
items.quote: Unidirectional airflow systems should provide a homogeneous air speed in a range of 0.36 – 0.54 m/s (guidance value) at the working position, unless otherwise scientifically justified in the CCS.
items.condition: unless otherwise scientifically justified in the CCS

items.statement: Airflow visualisation studies correlate with air speed measurements.
items.quote: Airflow visualization studies should correlate with the air speed measurement.

items.statement: The microbial contamination level of cleanrooms is determined during cleanroom qualification.
items.quote: The microbial contamination level of the cleanrooms should be determined as part of the cleanroom qualification.

items.statement: The number of microbial sampling locations for qualification is based on a documented risk assessment, room classification results, air visualisation studies and process/operations knowledge.
items.quote: The number of sampling locations should be based on a documented risk assessment and the results obtained from room classification, air visualization studies and knowledge of the process and operations to be performed in the area.

items.statement: Microbial qualification of cleanrooms covers both the at rest and in operation states.
items.quote: Qualification should include both “at rest” and “in operation” states.

items.statement: Grade A microbial qualification limit: no growth for air sample, settle plates and contact plates.

items.statement: Settle plates are exposed for the duration of operations and changed as needed after no more than 4 hours.
items.quote: Settle plates should be exposed for the duration of operations and changed as required after a maximum of 4 hours.

items.statement: Settle plate exposure time is based on recovery studies and does not let the media dry out.
items.quote: Exposure time should be based on recovery studies and should not allow desiccation of the media used.

items.statement: All methods listed for a grade in Table 2 are used when qualifying an area of that grade.
items.quote: All methods indicated for a specific grade in the table should be used for qualifying the area of that specific grade.

items.statement: If a tabulated method is not used or alternative methods are used, the approach is appropriately justified.
items.quote: If one of the methods tabulated is not used, or alternative methods are used, the approach taken should be appropriately justified.
items.condition: if a tabulated method is not used or alternatives are used

items.statement: Where technologies reporting results other than as CFU are used, the manufacturer scientifically justifies the limits applied and, where possible, correlates them to CFU.
items.quote: If different or new technologies are used that present results in a manner different from CFU, the manufacturer should scientifically justify the limits applied and where possible correlate them to CFU.
items.condition: if technologies reporting results other than CFU are used

items.statement: For personnel gowning qualification, the contact plate and glove print limits of Table 6 apply.
items.quote: For the qualification of personnel gowning, the limits given for contact plates and glove prints in Table 6 should apply.

items.statement: Sampling methods do not create a contamination risk to manufacturing operations.
items.quote: Sampling methods should not pose a risk of contamination to the manufacturing operations.

items.statement: Cleanrooms and clean air equipment are requalified periodically following defined procedures.
items.quote: The requalification of cleanrooms and clean air equipment should be carried out periodically following defined procedures.

items.statement: Requalification includes at minimum: classification (total particle concentration), final filter integrity test, airflow volume measurement, verification of pressure differences between rooms, and air velocity test.
items.quote: The requalification should include at a minimum the following: i. cleanroom classification (total particle concentration), ii. integrity test of final filters, iii. airflow volume measurement, iv. verification of air pressure difference between rooms, and v. air velocity test

items.statement: For grades B, C and D, the air velocity test during requalification is performed according to a risk assessment documented in the CCS.
items.quote: For grade B, C and D the air velocity test should be performed according to a risk assessment documented as part of the CCS.

items.statement: The air velocity test is always done for filling zones supplied with unidirectional airflow (e.g. filling terminally sterilised products, or background to grade A and RABS).
items.quote: However, it is required for filling zones supplied with unidirectional airflow (e.g. when filling terminally sterilised products or background to grade A and RABS).
items.condition: filling zones supplied with unidirectional airflow

items.statement: For grades with non-unidirectional airflow, recovery testing replaces velocity testing in requalification.
items.quote: For grades with non- unidirectional airflow, a measurement of recovery testing should replace velocity testing).

items.statement: Grade A and B areas are requalified at intervals of no more than 6 months.
items.quote: The maximum time interval for requalification of grade A & B areas, is 6 months.

items.statement: Grade C and D areas are requalified at intervals of no more than 12 months.
items.quote: The maximum time interval for requalification of grade C & D areas, is 12 months.

items.statement: Appropriate requalification, including at least the listed tests, is also done after remedial action for an out-of-compliance equipment or facility condition, or after changes to equipment, facility or processes as appropriate.
items.quote: Appropriate requalification consisting of at least the above tests should also be carried out following completion of remedial action implemented to rectify an out of compliance equipment or facility condition or after changes to equipment, facility or processes as appropriate.

items.statement: The significance of a change to cleanrooms or clean air equipment is decided through the change management process.
items.quote: The significance of a change should be determined through the change management process.

items.statement: Cleanrooms are thoroughly cleaned and disinfected following a written programme.
items.quote: They should be cleaned and disinfected thoroughly in accordance with a written programme.

items.statement: Cleaning to remove surface contamination is done before disinfection.
items.quote: For disinfection to be effective, prior cleaning to remove surface contamination should be performed.

items.statement: Cleaning programmes effectively remove disinfectant residues.
items.quote: Cleaning programmes should effectively remove disinfectant residues.

items.statement: More than one type of disinfecting agent is used so that, where modes of action differ, their combined use is effective against bacteria and fungi.
items.quote: More than one type of disinfecting agent should be employed to ensure that where they have different modes of action, their combined usage is effective against bacteria and fungi.

items.statement: Cleanroom disinfection includes periodic use of a sporicidal agent.
items.quote: Disinfection should include the periodic use of a sporicidal agent.

items.statement: Regular monitoring assesses the disinfection programme's effectiveness and detects changes in microbial flora types (e.g. organisms resistant to the current regime).
items.quote: Monitoring should be undertaken regularly in order to assess the effectiveness of the disinfection programme and to detect changes in types of microbial flora (e.g. organisms resistant to the disinfection regime currently in use).

items.statement: The cleanroom disinfection process is validated.
items.quote: The disinfection process should be validated.

items.statement: Disinfectant validation studies show suitability and effectiveness in the specific manner of use and on the surface material type (or representative material if justified), and support in-use expiry periods of prepared solutions.
items.quote: Validation studies should demonstrate the suitability and effectiveness of disinfectants in the specific manner in which they are used and on the type of surface material, or representative material if justified, and should support the in-use expiry periods of prepared solutions.
